body.statement: If \(\kappa=0\), then \(e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]\) on the exact class \(\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), and \[R_n\asymp\rho_{n,0}=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\] for every \(n\ge2\), with no logarithmic factor at \(\alpha+\beta=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\). This is the explicit exactly uniform bounded-overlap comparator slice: its rate equals KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, but both inequalities hold on the singleton uniform design and the lower inequality is proved with legal full-support Bernoulli laws rather than the comparator's perforated-support construction.
body.justification: The bounded-overlap reduction is the required sanity check and forces a new same-class lower bound rather than a citation to an inadmissible support-modified witness.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE proves this polynomial frontier over a density-qualified class whose displayed least-favorable density is uniform only on a perforated set, not over the singleton uniform design distribution.
body.consumer: Researchers comparing causal estimators under fixed uniform random design receive the established bounded-overlap benchmark as an exact special case of the new frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: For \(\kappa=0\) and \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), prove the stated higher-order upper bound and the matching nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform-design class, including the no-log conclusion at \(\alpha+\beta=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).
obligation.obstruction: The published perforated-support lower construction is not a member of the frozen exact-uniform model, while the supplied full-support construction has only one-observation cancellation and lacks the required product-mixture distance bound. The first-order estimator proved here is slower than the displayed comparator throughout part of the rough-nuisance region and therefore cannot establish the claimed upper inequality there.
obligation.attempted: I proved the overlap reduction \(e_P\in[1/4,1/2]\), the exact-uniform Bernoulli oracle converse, and the total first-order estimator. These close the displayed comparator theorem when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\). I also checked the squared-frame cancellation route in the rough slice, but its unresolved shared-sign product terms prevent both the exact-class nuisance lower bound and a proof of the theorem as stated.
obligation.partial_result:
At \(\kappa=0\), the model assumptions directly give
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
\]
for every \(x\).  Let \(s=\alpha+\beta\).  The established oracle lower bound and first-order estimator imply
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-\min\{\gamma,s\}/(2\min\{\gamma,s\}+d)}.
\]
In particular, if \(s\ge\gamma\), then \(R_n\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\).  In this regime the second term in \(\rho_{n,0}\) is no larger than the first, so the stated bounded-overlap formula is proved, with no logarithmic factor.  The asserted sharper conclusion for every \(s<\gamma\), including its nuisance-dominated lower bound on exactly uniform design, is not supplied by these arguments.
